US11297348B2.title: Implicit transform settings for coding a block of pixels

E1_implicit.description: the transform is derived implicitly, without explicit signalling
E1_implicit.evidence: Claim 1: 'deriving a transform setting based on a block processing setting for the block of pixels' and 'wherein deriving the transform setting comprises selecting a transform mode from a plurality of transform modes based on the block processing setting'. The transform mode is derived, not signalled.

E3_per_axis.description: the horizontal and the vertical axis are predicted separately
E3_per_axis.evidence: Claim 1 and claim 10: 'the position is used to determine a transform type from the set of transform types for a horizontal transform, and when the horizontal splitting orientation is used, the position is used to determine the transform type for a vertical transform'. The horizontal and the vertical transform are chosen separately, but from the block's partitioning orientation and the transformed sub-block's position, not from the neighbourhood's geometry.

E2_geometry.description: the derivation reads the geometry of a neighbourhood of reconstructed samples

E4_margin.description: the encoder may take a less optimal transform, at a rate-distortion cost, to avoid signalling the correction

E5_learned.description: the prediction comes from a trained or learned model

E6_correction.description: a correction is signalled relative to a prediction

US11297348B2.notes: The claim is about a sub-block transform: the transform type is a function of the SBT partitioning, the sub-block's position and the block's size. There is no geometry of reconstructed samples, no learned model, and no rate-distortion margin in the claims.

US11134275B2.title: Implicit transform type signalling

E1_implicit.description: the transform is derived implicitly, without explicit signalling
E1_implicit.evidence: Claim 1: 'in response to determining that the filtering process is applied on the current block, performing, based on the filtering process, a primary transform for a transform block that is partitioned from the current block'. The decoder performs the transform; the transform mode is not signalled per block.

E2_geometry.description: the derivation reads the geometry of a neighbourhood of reconstructed samples
E2_geometry.evidence: Claim 1: 'the filtering process adjusts inter prediction samples of the current block based on neighboring reconstructed samples of the current block'. The neighbouring reconstructed samples are read, but they are used to filter the prediction, and the transform is chosen from the filtering mode and the block's size, not from the samples' geometry.

E3_per_axis.description: the horizontal and the vertical axis are predicted separately
E3_per_axis.evidence: Claim 3: 'the primary transform is a type-7 discrete sine transform (DST-7) mode for a horizontal transform that is applied to the transform block responsive to a width of the current block being smaller than or equal to a threshold value, the primary transform is the DST-7 mode for a vertical transform that is applied to the transform block responsive to a height of the current block being smaller than or equal to the threshold value'. The horizontal and the vertical transforms are chosen separately, but each is a function of the block's width or height, not of a prediction.

E4_margin.description: the encoder may take a less optimal transform, at a rate-distortion cost, to avoid signalling the correction

E5_learned.description: the prediction comes from a trained or learned model

E6_correction.description: a correction is signalled relative to a prediction

US11134275B2.notes: The transform is a function of the filtering mode, the CIIP or PDPC mode, the block's width and height, and whether the neighbours are intra coded. The neighbouring blocks' coding mode is a form of neighbourhood context, but it is their prediction mode, not the geometry of their reconstructed samples.

E1_implicit.description: the transform is derived implicitly, without explicit signalling
E1_implicit.evidence: Claim 1: 'a video encoder for encoding at least a block in a picture by selecting a transform to apply to a residue of the block from a set of two or more transforms, wherein the transform is selected responsive to an inter prediction mode used to predict at least one reference for the block'. The transform is selected by the encoder and derived by the decoder, not signalled per block.

E2_geometry.description: the derivation reads the geometry of a neighbourhood of reconstructed samples

E3_per_axis.description: the horizontal and the vertical axis are predicted separately
E3_per_axis.evidence: Claim 4: 'wherein the transforms in the set are any of separable or non-separable, and horizontal and vertical directions of the transforms are capable of being different when the transforms are separable'. The horizontal and the vertical transform are separately identifiable.

E5_learned.description: the prediction comes from a trained or learned model
E5_learned.evidence: Claim 3: 'wherein the set of transforms is determined by at least one of: (i) using training data, and (ii) choosing a subset of a family of transforms'. The transform set is determined by training data.

That is the closest art to the whole of the disclosure, and it is twenty years old.

US20240040151A1.title: Coefficient-based transform and mode signaling

E1_implicit.description: the transform is derived implicitly, without explicit signalling
E1_implicit.evidence: Claim 7: 'when the determined pattern matches a pre-defined pattern, determining whether a transform type used in coding matches a default transform type associated with the pre-defined pattern; and when the determined pattern matches the pre-determined pattern, the transmitted coded data of the transform unit omits an identification of a transform type applied during the transforming'. The transform type is inferred at the decoder and not signalled.

E2_geometry.description: the derivation reads the geometry of a neighbourhood of reconstructed samples
E2_geometry.evidence: The abstract: 'based on the spatial locations of decoded coefficients, the spatial patterns of coefficients, or the correlation with the coefficients in neighboring blocks, various syntax elements such as the transform type and related flags/indices ... may be disabled or constrained'. The correlation with the neighbouring blocks' coefficients is the neighbourhood context.

E6_correction.description: a correction is signalled relative to a prediction
E6_correction.evidence: Claim 2: 'comparing a transform type applied during the transforming to a default transform type defined by the coding protocol and, when a transform type applied during the transforming and the default transform type defined by the coding protocol are the same, omitting an identifier of the transform type from the coded data'. The signalling is relative to a default, and it is omitted when the default matches.

E3_per_axis.description: the horizontal and the vertical axis are predicted separately

E4_margin.description: the encoder may take a less optimal transform, at a rate-distortion cost, to avoid signalling the correction

E5_learned.description: the prediction comes from a trained or learned model

US20240040151A1.notes: Priority 2022-07-28, so this is the most recent reference. It derives the transform type, and a range of other syntax elements, from the pattern of the decoded coefficients and their correlation with the neighbouring blocks, and it omits the signalling when the inferred value matches a default. The inference is from the coefficients rather than from the reconstructed pixels' geometry, and the omission is a match against a default rather than a rate-distortion trade.
